ai.title: NVIDIA Releases Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB: An Open Small Language Model for Local Voice Agents, Game Characters and Robots
ai.brief: 5 Bolt E4B 4GB , an open small language model for fast conversational agents. It targets voice assistants, game NPCs and robot interfaces running locally on RTX, Jetson and Spark hardware. The model is post-trained from Google’s Gemma 4 E4B using reinforcement learning only. For developers, this is agent behavior in about 4GB of VRAM. That leaves room for speech and vision models. TL;DR Size: 8B total parameters , 4B effective, 64K context. Runs on: GeForce RTX, Jetson, RTX Spark and DGX Spark. 3 GB VRAM on RTX in NVIDIA tests. 5-4B and Nemotron 3 Nano 4B (NVIDIA-measured). 5-4B. 1. 5 Bolt E4B? 5 Bolt E4B is a small language model from NVIDIA that powers local conversational agents. It combines natural dialogue with multi-turn tool calling. NVIDIA lists 3 target workloads: device and voice assistants, interactive characters, and embedded or industrial agents.

sec.title: Capcom Data Breach Exposes 11.7 Million Email Addresses
sec.brief: S. CISA adds Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog Japanese gaming company Capcom has disclosed a data breach discovered on October 19 involving its CAPCOM ID service, which provides access to online services and games. As of October 22, attackers stole 11,774,247 email addresses, along with account details including creation dates, last login dates, login counts, and the IP addresses used for the latest logins. ” reads the company’s notice . “Number of leaked email addresses and system-specific identification information: 11,774,247 (worldwide total)” In 43 cases, hackers exposed date of birth, gender, country/region, and nickname. Capcom also reported that attackers illegally changed passwords on 196 accounts, and the company has already reset them. The company said the incident exposed personal information belonging to a small number of individuals.
